scenario.situation: The Market District sprawls across a reinforced platform suspended between the void-scarred ruins of what was once a thriving commercial sector on Aeon, humanity's adopted homeworld after the Collapse scattered them across the scattered systems. The air here tastes metallic, tinged with the subtle wrongness of void corruption—a persistent reminder that reality itself frays at the edges on worlds like this. Overhead, the pale sun of the Aeon system struggles through atmospheric haze, casting everything in perpetual twilight. This neutral trade hub exists in the liminal space between faction territories: the Sovereign Nexus controls the northern districts with their authoritarian order, the Archivists maintain their knowledge vaults to the east, and the Freeborn networks operate openly in zones like this where no single power dominates. Three vendors have established operations here, each representing different economic philosophies. Against the eastern wall stands a gleaming S4CU Nexus Vending Terminal, its holographic interface cycling through inventory displays—but its Soulcredit verification scanner glows an unforgiving red, the Nexus's way of ensuring only the morally compliant can access their resources. Nearby, an independent trader named Kael Voss has spread his wares across a makeshift stall: ritual components, preserved food, trade goods salvaged from pre-Collapse ruins on distant planetoids. He eyes every passerby with practiced neutrality, his greeting painted on a weathered sign: 'All Welcome, No Questions Asked.' Hovering silently near the southern entrance, SD-7, an automated supply drone, offers basic provisions with mechanical efficiency—no authentication, no judgment, just commerce. In the back chambers, accessible through a pressure-sealed door, two ritual altars await those seeking to stabilize their Raw Seeds before void degradation renders them hollow. The first is a modest Freeborn altar, its stone surface carved with simple resonance patterns—functional, unpretentious, open to anyone who can pay the Spark fee. The second is a masterwork: a Nexus-maintained sanctified altar of breathtaking geometric precision, its void channels humming with controlled power, offering superior success rates for those skilled enough to harness it. Your party has converged on this hub with a singular purpose: to stress-test every economic mechanism this place offers. Some of you carry Raw Seeds pulsing with unstable energy, counting down the cycles until they degrade into dangerous Hollow variants. Others have currency weighing heavy in your pockets—Breath, Drip, Grain, Spark—the energy-based economy that replaced pre-Collapse money when humanity learned to harness void energy for survival. Soulcredit scores vary wildly among you: one of your number bears the stigma of a deeply negative rating, locked out of Nexus resources; another walks the borderline; two others have earned enough moral standing to access premium services. The question before you is simple but multifaceted: Can you navigate this hub's complex economic ecosystem? Will resource pooling via transfers overcome access barriers? Can low-quality altars serve those locked out of premium facilities? How many Seeds can you successfully attune before your Spark reserves run dry? The Market District awaits your economic experimentation.

altars.description: A simple stone altar with modest void resonance patterns carved into its surface. Quality 3 provides +1 bonus to attunement rituals (DC 20 becomes DC 19). Open to all users, no restrictions.

An exquisitely crafted master altar with pristine void channels and flawless geometry. Quality 8 provides +3 bonus to attunement rituals (DC 20 becomes DC 17). Maintained by the Sovereign Nexus but accessible to qualified users.
